page: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with symmetric multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and FMA. The instance comes equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources include 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the middle tier of general compute servers, highlighted by a strong top-25% result in stress-ng single-core execution at 2936.98. Multi-core performance aligns with expected midrange metrics, scoring 23301.5 in stress-ng multi-core and 8912.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory throughput demonstrates stable mid-tier bandwidth, delivering 117.03 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 77.42 GB/sec for write operations on 256 MB blocks. In-memory and caching benchmarks reflect reliable performance, achieving 15.29 million Redis SET operations per second and 8.45 GB/sec static web serving throughput. A notable limitation surfaces in heavier natural language processing tasks: prompt processing for a medium 7B parameter LLM registers at 18.38 tokens per second, falling into the bottom 25% bracket due to the lack of hardware vector acceleration extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX.

The dedicated core allocation and balanced memory ratio offer consistent execution efficiency without the resource contention typical of shared-core configurations. Integrating fast local NVMe storage directly with 32.0 GB of memory makes the voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd instance suitable for production web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, microservices backends, and moderate relational database workloads.
description: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is a general-purpose Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 32.0 GB of system memory and 160 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, along with one public IPv4 address. Benchmarks demonstrate solid midrange performance, distinguished by strong top-quartile single-core stress-ng throughput, alongside consistent results across Geekbench multi-core testing, compilation tasks, and Redis key-value operations. System memory bandwidth remains stable across both cached and uncached block tests. However, the lack of AVX-512 and matrix extensions reduces efficiency for larger LLM prompt processing. Delivering predictable resource allocation with a 1:4 compute-to-memory balance and bundled fast NVMe storage, this instance is well suited for web serving, build automation, caching tiers, and medium-scale relational database engines.
